$comment: Dantika Dental Studio: a fictional two-branch dental clinic in Bengaluru, and the single source of truth for the demo. The brain and the page both read this file (and bookings.json). Nothing the front desk says about prices, rules, hours, dentists or slots comes from anywhere else. Dates are never written down: a booking names a week relative to the current one (0 = this week, Monday first) and a weekday, so the calendar is full whatever day the demo runs.

cbct_referral.title: CBCT needs a referral or a consultation
cbct_referral.text: A CBCT scan is taken only with a referral from a dentist, or after a consultation with one of our dentists. If you have neither, we book a consultation first; the dentist decides whether the scan is needed.

opg_recent.title: Wisdom tooth surgery needs a recent OPG
opg_recent.text: Surgical wisdom-tooth removal needs an OPG taken in the last six months, so the surgeon can see how the tooth sits. If you don't have one, book the OPG first; it can be on the same day, before the surgery.

rct_sittings.title: Root canals take three sittings
rct_sittings.text: A root canal is three sittings of an hour each with Dr Kavitha, 7 to 14 days apart. We book the first sitting and pencil in the next two at the same time of day; you can move them later.

same_day_emergency.title: Emergencies are seen the same day
same_day_emergency.text: Emergency slots can be booked for today, from 30 minutes from now. Other appointments need at least an hour's notice. On Sundays the clinic is closed; call the emergency line.

cancellation.text: You can cancel or reschedule for free up to 24 hours before your appointment. Within 24 hours there is a ₹300 late-change fee, which we waive for emergency visits. A missed appointment without notice is charged ₹500. Scans and X-rays can be cancelled free up to 2 hours before. Each appointment can be changed online twice; after that, please call the desk.
cancellation.rct_text: A root canal's next sitting has to stay within 14 days of the one before it, so the tooth stays sealed. Moving it later needs Dr Kavitha's go-ahead; we arrange a callback.

eating.title: Eating before your visit
eating.general: Eat normally before most visits. Brush before you come.

by_service.consult: Eat normally. Bring any previous X-rays or prescriptions.
by_service.checkup: Eat normally and brush before you come.
by_service.emergency: Eat if you can; don't skip a meal because of the pain. Bring a list of any painkillers you've taken today.
by_service.scaling: Eat normally beforehand. Your gums may feel tender for a day or two.
by_service.filling: Have a light meal 1 to 2 hours before. You may be numb for 2 to 3 hours afterwards.
by_service.rct: Have a proper meal 1 to 2 hours before: you will be numb for 2 to 3 hours afterwards.
by_service.extraction: Have a light meal about 2 hours before. Please don't come on an empty stomach.
by_service.wisdom: Have a light meal about 2 hours before, and arrange for someone to take you home.
by_service.aligner: Eat normally and brush well; we take digital scans of your teeth.
by_service.whitening: Eat normally. Skip tea, coffee and other coloured food and drink for 48 hours after.
by_service.implant: Eat normally. Bring any previous X-rays or scans.
by_service.opg: No preparation needed. Remove earrings, nose pins and hair clips before the scan.
by_service.cbct: No fasting needed. Remove all jewellery, hair clips and removable dentures before the scan.

by_service.scaling: Some sensitivity for a few days is normal. Use a sensitivity toothpaste and lukewarm water.
by_service.filling: Wait until the numbness wears off before eating, about 2 hours. Avoid very hard food on that side for a day.
by_service.rct: Avoid chewing on that side until your last sitting and crown. A temporary filling may feel rough; that is normal.
by_service.extraction: Bite on the gauze for 30 to 45 minutes. For 24 hours: no spitting, no straws, no smoking, and cold soft food only.
by_service.wisdom: Bite on the gauze for 45 minutes. Use cold packs on the cheek for the first day, eat soft cold food, and don't spit, rinse hard or use a straw for 24 hours. Stitches are checked after 7 days.
by_service.whitening: Follow a 'white diet' for 48 hours: no tea, coffee, red sauces, turmeric curries or colas. Mild sensitivity for a day is normal.
by_service.aligner: Nothing special; your plan and smile preview are emailed within two working days.

payment.title: Payment
payment.text: We take UPI, debit and credit cards, and cash. Treatments of ₹10,000 or more can be paid in no-cost EMIs on most major credit cards. You pay at the desk after each visit and get an itemised bill every time.

insurance.title: Insurance
insurance.text: We are not on any cashless dental network. We give you an itemised bill, prescription and treatment notes for every visit, so you can claim reimbursement from your insurer if your policy covers outpatient dental care. Check your policy's dental cover before your visit.

what_to_bring.title: What to bring
what_to_bring.text: Your phone (we confirm visits by SMS), any previous X-rays, scans or prescriptions, and a list of medicines you take. Please arrive 10 minutes early for your first visit.

late_arrival.title: Running late
late_arrival.text: If you're more than 15 minutes late we may need to move you to the next free slot so the next patient isn't kept waiting. Call the branch if you're running late.

children.title: Children
children.text: We see children from age 4 for check-ups, cleanings and fillings with Dr Rahul or Dr Farah. A parent must stay with children under 18.

sunday.title: Sundays and holidays
sunday.text: Both branches are closed on Sundays. For a dental emergency on a Sunday, call our emergency line, +91 98804 71800, and the on-call dentist calls you back.

clinical.$comment: What the front desk must not answer. Anything here goes to a dentist through a callback, never as advice.
topics: which painkiller or antibiotic to take, or how much
whether to stop a medicine before treatment (blood thinners, diabetes medicine)
pain after a procedure that is getting worse
clinical.red_flags: Swelling spreading to the eye, jaw or neck, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or a high fever: go to the nearest hospital emergency department or call 112 now.
